item.title: The bin men do not do their job, 29th September
item.description:
The main issue is that the bin collection team repeatedly leaves the communal bin area in a poor and unacceptable condition after carrying out their collections. They do not appear to clean up after themselves, and the area is often left looking messy and unhygienic. There are occasions when the bin chambers are already full and there is no space for the remaining bins. Rather than properly managing the situation and leaving the area clean, the additional bins are simply left outside of the bin chamber. This means residents are left with bins obstructing the area and rubbish being exposed. We also regularly find bins left open after collections. While residents obviously have a responsibility to dispose of their rubbish properly, the collection team should still be leaving the bins and surrounding area in an appropriate condition after they have completed their work. More concerningly, the communal doors have also been damaged on several occasions during the collection process. This has happened repeatedly and is unacceptable. The collection team should be carrying out their work without causing damage to the building or its communal facilities. I would therefore like this complaint to be passed on and escalated. The bin area should be left clean, tidy and safe after every collection. At present, this is not consistently happening, and it is having a negative impact on the cleanliness and appearance of our building.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Chatham Street, Walworth, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Couch outside communal area, 29th September
item.description:
There is a constant fly tipping problem in our block. I am sick and tired of walking out of our main communal door, to see mattresses, TV’s, Couches, beds, cupboards& wardrobes. It is an actual mess, they continue to do this as there is no repercussion. It is disgusting! Alongside others that actually pay the council to remove things legally, enough is enough. This needs to be looked in to. These items attract a lot of foxes and species that make it even worse than it is. This issue has been going on for more than a year.
